The House of Hill (Sam and Simon Hill) defeated the Haughty Troupe when Munchy Man tapped to Sam Hill's King of the Hill (cross-face chicken wing).

matches.note: BookFace defeated Raucous.

No finish: the match was interrupted before a decision by an unscheduled attack from Kid Koala, eKid Nah and Kangarry Roo (the Marsupials of Mayhem, making their RLW debut), who then stood down when the House of Hill (Sam, Simon and J.J. Hill) ran in to confront them.

note: This broadcast's own closing segment also reveals the format of RLW's inaugural Red Crown Tournament and previews (without wrestling) the participants of a triple-threat quarterfinal to be held on Slamtrack 3; those previewed entrants (Go-Go Spectacular, Ivan Dalkichev, Nathan Fear) are not structured as appearances on this show since no match involving them takes place on it.

name: Rush Hour

date.source: Posted to RLW's own RLW Live! sub-forum; no in-story date is given in the broadcast text itself, so the date follows the thread's own posting date.

matches.note: J-MAX (Roger Stevens and Yoshikazu YAZ), managed by Lisa Loeh, defeated Johnny Dorn and BookFace.
No finish: both men knocked each other unconscious with steel chairs after the bout was already called off; no winner was declared.
Kid Koala was eliminated by disqualification for using a weapon; The Second Coming then defeated Go-Go Spectacular to become the new #1 contender to the Red Crown Championship.
Ivan Dalkichev defeated Russ Spackler with a second-rope Titan Bomb to become RLW's first-ever Red Crown Champion.

note: RLW's own first internet pay-per-view, crowning its inaugural Red Crown Champion; Leyenda de Ocho, an already-established fwrestling.com character, serves as guest color commentator throughout.

matches.stipulation: Open Battle Royal (fifteen entrants; last remaining is next in line for the Red Crown Championship after Mass Transit)
matches.note: Hittora won the battle royal, becoming the new #1 contender heading into Mass Transit; a fifteenth entrant, Derrick Allen, is eliminated in the broadcast's own text but never separately registered elsewhere in the held record and is not minted.

note: The broadcast ends with Red Crown Champion Ivan Dalkichev interrupting the show to attack Eric Dane, Hittora and The Second Coming; Nathan Fear threatens to pull Dalkichev out of RLW before Dalkichev himself tears up the contract, setting up a Mass Transit main event RLW's own corpus never resolves (see this wing's own registry note on Mass Transit).

name: Mass Transit

date.source: No show-thread was ever completed for this show; this date is when its own pre-match promo threads (Match Threads sub-forum) begin. RLW's own operator, in a series of OOC progress-update posts running from 27 June to 3 August 2015, states the write-up was repeatedly delayed by real-life circumstances and was never finished before RLW's own hiatus announcement of 3 November 2015 admits the show was never released.

notes: Five pre-match promo threads survive (Hittora v. Jessica Cross; a No-DQ match, El Habanero v. Victor Vacio; a Tables match, Go-Go Spectacular v. Emevlas Stastias; a Triple Threat, Eric Dane v. Dick Fury v. Brad Andrews; and a main event billed Ivan Dalkichev (c) v. The Second Coming for the Red Crown Championship), but no show script, and therefore no result for any of these advertised matches, was ever posted. RLW's own operator confirms in the held record's last dated document (the hiatus announcement) that the show was never completed.
